spec.title: Tool error rate (range)
spec.description: Stopgap: excludes known LLM model names accidentally recorded as tool_name (instrumentation bug). Fix the root cause in your tool-call recording code when possible.

spec.title: Tool latency by tool (p50 / p95 / p99)
spec.description: topk(5) per quantile keeps only the 5 worst tools per line — previously ~60 series made this unreadable. Exclude filter is the same LLM-name stopgap as the error-rate panels.

spec.title: Root error rate (range)
spec.description: Errors as a % of total root requests (was a raw error count).

spec.title: Tokens by component (stacked, input vs output)
Recent error/warning logs
spec.description: If this panel is empty, check the exact OTLP label name Grafana Cloud assigned to service.name.

spec.title: Request error rate by root span
Traces for this session (click a row to open)
Recent traces (click a row to open)
Request latency by root span (p50 / p95 / p99)
End-to-end session latency (p50 / p95 / p99) — root span
spec.description: Uses request_duration_ms_milliseconds_bucket (same source as Request Health), aggregated across all request_name values. This IS your real session latency — no separate metric needed.

spec.title: Latency by phase: LLM call vs Tool execution (p95)
spec.description: LLM phase now uses the real gen_ai_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket metric (converted seconds->ms). Queue wait removed — no metric exists for it yet.

spec.title: Time-in-phase share (stacked %, avg duration)
spec.description: Average LLM vs Tool duration, stacked, using real gen_ai + tool_call metrics. Queue wait removed.

spec.title: LLM call latency by model (p50 / p95 / p99)
spec.description: New panel using real gen_ai_client_operation_duration_seconds_bucket, labeled by gen_ai_response_model. Direct visibility into which model is slow — didn't exist before.

spec.title: Token usage per LLM call (p50 / p95) by model & type
spec.description: New panel using gen_ai_client_token_usage_bucket, labeled gen_ai_token_type (input/output) and gen_ai_response_model. Shows distribution per CALL, unlike llm_tokens_total which only shows throughput — this catches individual oversized prompts.
